claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and biblical scholar, born c. 185 and died c. 253-254.
Origen was born in Alexandria, Egypt, and later founded the Christian School of Caesarea.
Origen's commentary on 1 Corinthians survives only in fragments.
The fragments of Origen's commentary on 1 Corinthians were preserved in catenas (chains of quotations from earlier commentators compiled by later writers).
The fragments of Origen's commentary on 1 Corinthians were edited and published by C. Jenkins in the Journal of Theological Studies, volumes 9 and 10 (1908).
The fragments cover most of the epistle of 1 Corinthians, from chapter one to chapter sixteen.

The commentary contains information about various early Christian groups and practices, including references to Ophites, Montanists, heretics who used the Creed, and details about the Eucharistic service.
The commentary contains Origen's allusions to predecessor(s) in the exegesis of 1 Corinthians.
The authorship of the fragments attributed to Origen has been disputed based on stylometric analysis, with one study suggesting Gregory of Nyssa or another third party as possible author.
